headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared retrieval/workspace paths; OpenBB’s MCP/API surfaces can amplify cross-agent misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj ingests indexed documents and can use optional web search; OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/API surfaces and a “connect once, consume everywhere” pattern. If OpenBB consumes Khoj outputs or shared files, attacker-controlled content in notes/docs could be treated as instructions. No explicit provenance filtering is shown, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange content through a shared file, MCP, or API bridge
IF OpenBBTerminal parses Khoj-produced text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Khoj outputs into OpenBB
Add a manual review step before any cross-agent copy/paste
Restrict shared folders to read-only exports
Prefix all transferred content with provenance labels
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and can call APIs/MCP servers. If they share a workspace or exchange files, sensitive notes or financial data could leak across the pair. The profiles do not show isolation or DLP, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or exported files
IF either agent forwards shared content to an external API or MCP server
mitigations: Separate workspaces for notes and finance data
Turn off automatic file import/export between agents
Use per-agent service accounts and credentials
Review outbound API destinations before use
requires-engineering: implement DLP or redaction on shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj cannot write the filesystem and OpenBBTerminal also cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, so direct write-write conflicts are limited. The main overlap is read/API access, which is not a strong mutable-resource conflict. Because OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and APIs, a small coordination risk remains if both target the same external resource.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external account or MCP resource
IF an operator manually grants both write-like access through a shared service
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only on shared resources
Avoid giving both agents the same OAuth principal
Stagger runs when touching the same external system
Document ownership of each mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj is a retrieval/chat agent that can surface indexed content, and OpenBBTerminal can consume APIs/MCP and act as a financial modeling front end. If OpenBB treats Khoj output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream analysis or actions. No verification layer is shown, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal uses Khoj-generated text as input without verification
IF downstream workflows act on the combined output for trading, reporting, or publishing
mitigations: Require source citations before reuse
Add a human verification step for any factual claim
Compare outputs against primary sources
Limit automation to draft-only workflows
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. If personal or regulated data is moved into OpenBB’s API/MCP workflows, retention or licensing obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document matching residency or retention controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF personal notes or regulated documents are exported from Khoj into OpenBB workflows
IF the operator stores the same data class under different retention or licensing rules
mitigations: Classify data before moving it between agents
Keep regulated data out of OpenBB unless approved
Review retention settings for both systems
Use separate storage for licensed and personal content
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
